title: Contract
description: A Janus contract: what a consumer demonstrated against a mock, recorded so a provider can be held to it (spec.md §2). Not a pact file — ADR 0011 names this its own format. Documents this schema treats as opaque objects are owned elsewhere and validated against their own schemas: shapes by design 2.2, the selection report by design 2.3, transport and endpoint descriptors by design 2.6.

$format.description: The format token. A writer MUST emit this as the document's first member, so a conformant file begins with the byte prefix '{"$format":' (spec.md §2.3). JSON Schema cannot express member order; the writer conformance test does.

$schema.description: Advisory: the schema this document claims to follow. Identifier only — a reader MUST NOT fetch it (spec.md §2.3).

interactions.description: In the order the consumer submitted them. Every interaction here was exercised successfully on every variant its selection required (spec.md §2.2) — a contract is never written otherwise.

Pacticipant.title: Pacticipant
Pacticipant.description: A named party. The member name and the path to 'name' are fixed by spec.md §3.1 so brokers already deployed read them correctly.

Interaction.title: Interaction
Interaction.description: One interaction: its shape recorded once, and the evidence of every variant that was exercised (spec.md §4). Identity is 'description' plus 'states' (spec.md §4.2).

description.description: What the interaction is, in the author's words. Unique within a contract for a given state list (spec.md §4.2).

states.description: Provider states this interaction requires, with their literal parameters and their variant bindings (spec.md §6). Bindings appear here once; their resolved values appear per variant.

parts.description: Part name -> slot name -> shape. Part and slot names are the transport and content components' business, never the kernel's (shape spec §3.6); this schema fixes only the nesting.

requires.description: Components this interaction cannot be matched without (spec.md §7). A verifier collects the union across interactions before it starts.

Transport.title: Transport
Transport.description: How the parts crossed the wire. An open descriptor: 'kind' and 'mode' are fixed here, everything else belongs to the transport component (design 2.6).

kind.description: Open vocabulary; an unknown kind is 'component-unavailable' naming it, never a silent skip.

mode.description: Whether the consumer answers a request ('passive') or emits a message ('emissive') — protocol spec §8.2.

State.title: State
State.description: A provider state. 'params' holds literal parameters; 'variant-params' holds bindings whose value depends on the running variant (variant semantics §6.2, whose schema owns their contents).

params.description: Literal parameters, as authored. A name appearing here MUST NOT also appear in 'variant-params' (variant semantics §6.2).

variant-params.description: Variant-bound parameter bindings. Each item is design 2.3's binding document; 'dimension' is always the resolved dimension id, never the author's shorthand (variant semantics §6.3).

ShapePart.title: ShapePart
ShapePart.description: One part's shapes: slot name -> shape node. Each value is design 2.2's shape document, opaque here.

Requirement.title: Requirement
Requirement.description: A component the interaction needs, at a major version or above (spec.md §7). Structured rather than an expression string, because a document that must be evaluated to be understood cannot be reviewed (ADR 0007's reasoning).

component.description: '<interface>/<name>', e.g. 'content/protobuf'. The interface half is an open vocabulary owned by design 2.6.

min-version.description: Lowest acceptable major version. Majors only: the protocol is coarse-grained by ADR 0002, and a contract that pins a patch is a contract that breaks on a bug fix.

RecordedSelection.title: RecordedSelection
RecordedSelection.description: Design 2.3's variant-selection document — the exercised variants and the report of how they were chosen — with the evidence this design adds. Members not named here belong to variant-selection.schema.json and are validated against it (spec.md §5.1).

variants.description: In recorded order, which is run order: a verifier replays exactly these, in this order, and never re-samples (variant semantics §5.1). Only exercised variants appear — the honesty rule.

report.description: Design 2.3's selection report. Recording it is what makes a contract self-describing about its own coverage.

RecordedVariant.title: RecordedVariant
RecordedVariant.description: One exercised variant: its identity from design 2.3, and the concrete values it produced. 'parts' is this design's addition to design 2.3's variant document (variant semantics §4.4).

id.description: The variant id. 'base', or the ';'-joined '<dimension-id>=<point>' renderings of the dimensions that differ from their default. Never a label (variant semantics §2.2).

assignment.description: The assignment is the truth and the id is its name; both are recorded so a variant stays interpretable against a shape that has since grown a dimension.

states.description: The interaction's states with this variant's parameters resolved (variant semantics §6.4). Resolved values only — bindings live on the interaction, never here.

parts.description: Part name -> slot name -> the concrete value produced. Keyed identically to the interaction's 'parts', so shape and evidence line up slot for slot.

ResolvedState.title: ResolvedState
ResolvedState.description: A state as this variant needs it. A parameter with no case and no default is absent — not null, not empty (variant semantics §6.4).

ValuePart.title: ValuePart
ValuePart.description: One part's recorded values: slot name -> slot value.

SlotValue.title: SlotValue
SlotValue.description: The value a slot carried, always wrapped. The wrapper is unconditional and never in-band: a bare value with a sibling tag would be ambiguous against user data that happens to have that member, which is the trap ADR 0007 and variant semantics §6.2 both refuse (spec.md §5.3).

content.description: The value, represented as 'encoded' says. Absent means the slot was empty; null means the slot carried a null.

encoded.description: How to read 'content': 'json' is the value as it stands, so a JSON body stays readable and addressable; 'text' is a string whose octets are its UTF-8 encoding; 'base64' is RFC 4648 §4 octets (ADR 0006).

content-type.description: The media type the part declared for this slot, when it had one. Recorded because a verifier hands it to the content component and must not re-derive it.

Metadata.title: Metadata
Metadata.description: How the file came to exist, and nothing that changes what a verifier does (spec.md §3.2). Deliberately outside the content-addressed identity, so an unchanged rebuild is not a new contract. MUST NOT carry 'pactSpecification' — a Janus contract conforms to no pact specification version (ADR 0011).

writer.description: What wrote the file: an open map of component name to version string.

created.description: RFC 3339. Volatile by nature: a writer producing reproducible output omits it (spec.md §3.2).
